run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:40:15Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real failure evidence: frontend-proxy's 'ingress' server spans return HTTP 504 after exactly ~15.0 s (its upstream timeout), matched one-for-one by 'router frontend egress' spans of the same duration. A complete trace shows the request was not failing inside frontend-proxy: the load generator's checkout POST hangs in frontend's POST /api/checkout (89.09 s) and in checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (89.08 s), which ends in checkout's 'orders publish' span erroring after 88.87 s with 'circuit breaker is open'. Checkout's own container logs show the same errors plus 'kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker' for topic orders from at least 01:41:32 onward. The Kafka dependency is where the fault condition lives: Deployment kafka in otel-demo runs 2 replicas of the demo Kafka image, both configured with the single-node KRaft identity KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093, both logging nodeId=1, and both continuously logging STALE_BROKER_EPOCH assignment failures while the kafka Service routes clients to both pod IPs. That condition predates the observed fault injection. Separately, chaos-mesh NetworkChaos experiments named otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-* were applied every minute from 01:59:44 to ~02:08:39 to pods checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l, kafka-ff7884766-xclnk and kafka-ff7884766-skk8d, and the frontend-proxy error-span rate rose in that same interval (from ~0.45/s to a 1.24/s peak, plus kafka i/o timeouts) and fell afterwards. Flag-based injection is ruled out (all flagd flags are off, kafkaQueueProblems = 0). Because the alert's rule definition and the annotation's 'current: 1.6' could not be retrieved, because telemetry only begins at 01:41:15 (events at 01:45:11), and because the mechanism linking the duplicate broker identity to topic unavailability is a strongly-supported hypothesis rather than a directly observed event, the conclusion is partial; the object the evidence points to is Deployment kafka in namespace otel-demo.

claims.text: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans are recorded as errors with http.status_code 504 / otel.status_code ERROR after ~15.0 s (15,000,546–15,001,929 µs), each paired with a 'router frontend egress' span of the same ~15.0 s whose status tags are error="true" and http.status_code "0" (12 spans around 01:49:58; 40 spans between 01:55:46 and 01:57:49).

Trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 (started 01:56:20Z) shows the chain via explicit parent references: load-generator user_checkout_single 15.44 s → load-generator POST 504 15.00 s → frontend-proxy ingress 504 15.00 s → frontend POST 15.00 s → frontend POST /api/checkout 89.09 s → executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 89.08 s → frontend client grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 89.08 s → checkout server oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 89.08 s → checkout 'orders publish' 88.87 s with otel.status_code ERROR and description 'circuit breaker is open'.

Checkout container logs in pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l contain repeated 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open', 'Failed to write message: kafka: Failed to produce message to topic orders: kafka server: Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker', and at 02:08:23Z 'client/metadata got error from broker 1 while fetching metadata: read tcp 100.96.1.134:53048->100.71.78.255:9092: i/o timeout'; the same class of failure is already present at 01:41:32Z–01:43:59Z.

frontend-proxy error spans: 5-minute rate of the 'ingress' error series is 0.45–0.50/s from 01:45:15 to 01:58:15, peaks at 1.2407/s at 02:05:15 and decays to 0.148/s at 02:14:15; the 'router frontend egress' error series is 0 before 01:59:15, peaks at 0.7704/s at 02:03:15 and is 0 again from 02:11:15 on.

Service-level 5-minute error-span rates show frontend rising from 0 to 1.0431/s at 02:00:15 and 2.9037/s at 02:05:15, while checkout stays roughly flat at 0.379–0.489/s over every point from 01:45:15 to 02:10:15.
Deployment kafka in namespace otel-demo is configured with spec.replicas 2 and reports readyReplicas 2 and availableReplicas 2, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka, RollingUpdate strategy.

Both kafka pods are owned by ReplicaSet kafka-ff7884766 and carry identical broker settings: pod kafka-ff7884766-skk8d (IP 100.96.2.21) and pod kafka-ff7884766-xclnk (IP 100.96.4.61) both have KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093, KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093 and KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092.

The kafka Service (ClusterIP 100.71.78.255, plaintext port 9092, selector opentelemetry.io/name=kafka) has both pod addresses in its endpoints: 100.96.2.21 (kafka-ff7884766-skk8d) and 100.96.4.61 (kafka-ff7884766-xclnk).

kafka-ff7884766-skk8d logs '[AssignmentsManager id=1] handleResponse: 50 assignments failed; global error: Response-level error: STALE_BROKER_EPOCH. Retrying.' every ~10 s from 01:52:50 to 01:53:59, and its metadata-log lines identify it as nodeId=1.

kafka-ff7884766-xclnk logs '[ControllerApis nodeId=1]' and '[QuorumController id=1]', repeats 'assignReplicasToDirs: event failed with StaleBrokerEpochException ... Expected broker epoch 17, but got broker epoch 10' every ~10 s from 02:07:45 to 02:08:45, and records '[QuorumController id=1] CreateTopics result(s): CreatableTopic(name='orders', numPartitions=1, replicationFactor=1, ...): TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS' at 02:07:42.

chaos-mesh NetworkChaos events show nine experiments named otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-{fkbbr,96js2,c88bd,tfpsw,t2rzv,fnppk,znv8m,j8wrs,dtxwx}: 'Experiment has started' at 01:59:44, 02:00:44, 02:01:44, 02:02:44, 02:03:44, 02:04:44, 02:05:44, 02:06:44 and 02:07:44, each with 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l', 'otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-xclnk' and 'otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-skk8d', followed ~55 s later by 'Time up according to the duration' and matching 'Successfully recover chaos' entries.

PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events in namespace otel-demo exist only from 01:59 onward (3 in minute 01:59, then 6 per minute for 02:00 through 02:07); no PodNetworkChaos event falls between 01:45:11 and 01:59.

All 22 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready, with container restartCount 0 for every pod except ad-554b849958-4chjq (restartCount 1); frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout and both kafka pods each show 0 restarts.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) has state ENABLED for adFailure, adHighCpu, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure, and every flag's defaultVariant is 'off' (kafkaQueueProblems off = 0).

Pod ad-554b849958-4chjq restarted at 01:57:56Z after its 'ad' container was terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 (startedAt 01:28:19, finishedAt 01:57:56); its container limits are cpu 50m / memory 450Mi (requests 10m / 225Mi) and its post-restart log lines are ordinary ad request handling.
The earliest sample returned for the frontend-proxy error-span series is 01:41:15Z even though the query window started at 00:40:15Z (source_start_at 2026-11-18T01:41:15Z).

Deepest supported cause: Deployment kafka (otel-demo) runs two brokers that both present the single-node KRaft identity declared by KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093 and both log nodeId=1, behind a Service that load-balances clients across both pod IPs; broker registration and partition assignment keep failing with STALE_BROKER_EPOCH and topic 'orders' is not available on the broker checkout reaches, so checkout's produce fails ('Request was for a topic or partition that does not exist on this broker' / 'circuit breaker is open'), checkout's PlaceOrder blocks ~89 s, frontend's /api/checkout blocks with it, and frontend-proxy times out at 15 s returning 504.

A second, chaos-mesh fault acted as an amplifier rather than the origin: per-minute NetworkChaos experiments named otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-* partitioned checkout-5dccddf8bb-vn95l from kafka-ff7884766-xclnk and kafka-ff7884766-skk8d between 01:59:44 and ~02:08:39, coinciding with checkout's kafka-metadata i/o timeout at 02:08:23, the appearance of 'router frontend egress' error spans (0 before 01:59:15) and the frontend-proxy error-span rate rising from ~0.45/s to a 1.24/s peak and then falling after the last experiment; the timing correlation does not by itself prove the added errors came from this experiment.

The checkout→kafka failure predates the recorded network chaos: checkout's produce errors are logged at 01:41:32Z and 01:43:36Z and a checkout 'orders publish' span errors with 'circuit breaker is open' in a trace starting 01:49:58Z, while the earliest recorded NetworkChaos application to these pods is 01:59:44Z, so the partition experiments cannot be the whole explanation of the alert that started at 01:40:15Z.

Flag-driven fault injection (e.g. kafkaQueueProblems) was considered as the cause of checkout's Kafka failures and rejected: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config is state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off', including kafkaQueueProblems (off = 0), and no flag in the file targets frontend-proxy or a 504 timeout.

The ad pod's OOMKilled restart was considered as the origin of the frontend-proxy 504s and rejected: checkout's Kafka produce failures are logged from 01:41:32Z, before ad's 01:57:56Z restart, and the full 504 trace f18dd56ad5afb108674a31c6c7770ed1 contains no ad span and terminates in checkout's 'orders publish' Kafka error rather than in ad or a frontend 500.

The exact metric behind the alert could not be reproduced: a 1-minute rate query filtered on span_name="ingress" for frontend-proxy errors returned a single all-zero series for the whole 01:40:15–02:10:15 range, which contradicts the by-span_name aggregation of the same metric that returned 0.45–1.24/s, so the 'current: 1.5999…' in the alert annotation is unverified.

frontend-proxy is not the only service with error spans in the window and its own pods are healthy: frontend reports 1.0431/s at 02:00:15 and 2.9037/s at 02:05:15 of its own error spans, checkout reports a steady 0.379–0.489/s, and ad reports 0.1315/s at 02:10:15 — the frontend-proxy reading therefore describes a propagated failure, not a fault confined to frontend-proxy.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule itself could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data both for {alertname="RequestErrorRate"} and with no filter (status no_data), so the alert's expression, threshold, evaluation window and the annotation value 'current: 1.5999999999999999' are unverified.

Telemetry coverage starts at 01:41:15Z (first frontend-proxy error sample; the query window began at 00:40:15Z) and the events dataset starts at 01:45:11Z (earliest event), so whether the checkout→kafka failures and the frontend-proxy 504s began before 01:41 and whether chaos-mesh experiments ran before 01:45:11 are unknown; the alert is dated 01:40:15Z, at or before that coverage boundary.

Change history is not integrated (change_history is listed as not_integrated), so when and by what Deployment kafka was set to 2 replicas, and when the chaos-mesh Schedule that spawns otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-* was created, cannot be established.

The chaos-mesh objects themselves could not be read (NetworkChaos and Schedule are not among the readable Kubernetes kinds), so their selectors, action (partition/loss/delay), duration and the Schedule's own name are known only from their events.

The frontend container's logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-djtdf returned no data with 0 lines read, so frontend's own error text is unknown and frontend's role is evidenced only by its spans and error-rate series.
A tool reading inconsistency remains unresolved: a 1-minute rate with an explicit span_name="ingress" filter returned only zeros while aggregating the same metric by span_name returned 0.45–1.24/s.

The metrics available under service_name="frontend-proxy" are only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket; http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no data for that service, so any Envoy/HTTP-level request-error series that might carry the alert's exact value is unknown.

The ad pod's OOMKilled restart (01:57:56Z, memory limit 450Mi) and its 0.1315/s error-span reading at 02:10:15 were recorded but not investigated further; whether ad served errors to callers after the restart is unknown.
No evidence was examined for end-user or customer impact beyond the load-generator spans that received 504s; downstream/business consequences are unverified.
next_steps: Compare Deployment kafka's replica count (currently 2) with its single-voter KRaft configuration (KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093) and decide whether one of the two identical-identity brokers should be removed or given a distinct node id and quorum entry.

Review the chaos-mesh Schedule in the chaos-mesh namespace that creates the otel-demo-checkout-kafka-network-partition-* experiments, including its cron, duration and pod selectors, and confirm whether it is intended to overlap the checkout/kafka path.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alert rule (query, threshold, for-duration) from the rule source so the annotation value 1.6 and the 01:40:15 onset can be matched to a concrete metric series.

Verify with Kafka metadata tooling (topic 'orders' partition leadership and broker registrations) whether the STALE_BROKER_EPOCH loop is what leaves the topic unavailable to checkout, since that mechanism is currently a hypothesis.
Re-check frontend application logs from a source that retains them (the current pod stream returned nothing) to confirm how /api/checkout requests were terminated.
